claim: Inhibiting high-voltage-activated calcium channels (HVACCs; CaV1/CaV2) is therapeutic for myriad cardiovascular and neurological diseases.
source: Inhibiting high-voltage-activated calcium channels (HVACCs; CaV1/CaV2) is therapeutic for myriad cardiovascular and neurological diseases.
evidence: This is a general statement about the therapeutic value of HVACC inhibition, drawing from established scientific knowledge in the field.

claim: Nb.F3 binds auxiliary HVACC CaVβ subunits.
source: Here, we engineered a genetically-encoded HVACC inhibitor by first isolating an immunized llama nanobody (nb.F3) that binds auxiliary HVACC CaVβ subunits.
evidence: The manuscript describes the isolation and characterization of nb.F3, including co-translocation assays and isothermal titration calorimetry showing binding to CaVβ subunits.

claim: Nb.F3 by itself is functionally inert.
source: Nb.F3 by itself is functionally inert, providing a convenient vehicle to target active moieties to CaVβ-associated channels.
evidence: The manuscript presents flow cytometry and electrophysiology data showing that nb.F3 does not affect channel trafficking or currents.

claim: CaV-aβlator ablated currents from diverse HVACCs reconstituted in HEK293 cells.
source: Nb.F3 fused to the catalytic HECT domain of Nedd4L (CaV-aβlator), an E3 ubiquitin ligase, ablated currents from diverse HVACCs reconstituted in HEK293 cells, and from endogenous CaV1/CaV2 channels in mammalian cardiomyocytes, dorsal root ganglion neurons, and pancreatic β cells.
evidence: The manuscript presents electrophysiology data showing elimination of currents from multiple HVACC types in HEK293 cells.

claim: CaV-aβlator ablated currents from endogenous CaV1/CaV2 channels in mammalian cardiomyocytes.
source: Nb.F3 fused to the catalytic HECT domain of Nedd4L (CaV-aβlator), an E3 ubiquitin ligase, ablated currents from diverse HVACCs reconstituted in HEK293 cells, and from endogenous CaV1/CaV2 channels in mammalian cardiomyocytes, dorsal root ganglion neurons, and pancreatic β cells.
evidence: The manuscript presents electrophysiology data from guinea pig cardiomyocytes showing elimination of L-type calcium currents.

claim: CaV-aβlator ablated currents from endogenous CaV1/CaV2 channels in dorsal root ganglion neurons.
source: Nb.F3 fused to the catalytic HECT domain of Nedd4L (CaV-aβlator), an E3 ubiquitin ligase, ablated currents from diverse HVACCs reconstituted in HEK293 cells, and from endogenous CaV1/CaV2 channels in mammalian cardiomyocytes, dorsal root ganglion neurons, and pancreatic β cells.
evidence: The manuscript presents calcium imaging and electrophysiology data from DRG neurons showing elimination of HVACC-mediated calcium influx.

claim: CaV-aβlator ablated currents from endogenous CaV1/CaV2 channels in pancreatic β cells.
source: Nb.F3 fused to the catalytic HECT domain of Nedd4L (CaV-aβlator), an E3 ubiquitin ligase, ablated currents from diverse HVACCs reconstituted in HEK293 cells, and from endogenous CaV1/CaV2 channels in mammalian cardiomyocytes, dorsal root ganglion neurons, and pancreatic β cells.
evidence: The manuscript presents calcium imaging data from pancreatic β cells showing elimination of glucose- and KCl-evoked calcium transients.

claim: In cardiomyocytes, CaV-aβlator redistributed CaV1.2 channels from dyads to Rab-7-positive late endosomes.
source: In cardiomyocytes, CaV-aβlator redistributed CaV1.2 channels from dyads to Rab-7-positive late endosomes.
evidence: The manuscript presents immunofluorescence data showing decreased colocalization of α1C with RyR2 and increased colocalization with Rab7.

claim: Small molecule HVACC inhibitors include CaV1 blockers (dihydropyridines, benzothiazepenes phenylalkylamines).
source: Small molecule HVACC inhibitors include CaV1 blockers (dihydropyridines, benzothiazepenes phenylalkylamines) and venom peptides that target CaV2.1 (ω-agatoxin), CaV2.2 (ω-conotoxin), and CaV2.3 (SNX-482) channels.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about existing HVACC inhibitors.

claim: Venom peptides target CaV2.1 (ω-agatoxin), CaV2.2 (ω-conotoxin), and CaV2.3 (SNX-482) channels.
source: Small molecule HVACC inhibitors include CaV1 blockers (dihydropyridines, benzothiazepenes phenylalkylamines) and venom peptides that target CaV2.1 (ω-agatoxin), CaV2.2 (ω-conotoxin), and CaV2.3 (SNX-482) channels.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about venom peptide HVACC inhibitors.

claim: Small-molecule HVACC blockers are typically widely distributed when introduced into an organism, leading to off-target effects.
source: When introduced into an organism, small-molecule HVACC blockers are typically widely distributed leading to off-target effects that can narrow the therapeutic window and, thereby, adversely impact therapy.
evidence: This is a general statement about the pharmacological properties of small molecule drugs, based on established knowledge.

claim: Genetically-encoded HVACC inhibitors can circumvent off-target effects because they can be selectively expressed in target tissues or cells.
source: Genetically-encoded HVACC inhibitors can circumvent off-target effects because they can be selectively expressed in target tissues or cells; thus, they may be useful alternatives or complements to small molecule therapy (Yang et al., 2013; Murata et al., 2004).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work on genetically-encoded inhibitors.

claim: There are seven distinct HVACCs (CaV1.1 - CaV1.4; CaV2.1 - CaV2.3).
source: There are seven distinct HVACCs (CaV1.1 - CaV1.4; CaV2.1 - CaV2.3) which exist in cells as multi-subunit complexes comprising pore-forming α1-subunits assembled with auxiliary proteins which include β, α2-δ, and γ subunits (Zamponi et al., 2015; Buraei and Yang, 2010; Dolphin, 2012).
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about HVACC classification, supported by citations.

claim: HVACCs exist in cells as multi-subunit complexes comprising pore-forming α1-subunits assembled with auxiliary proteins which include β, α2-δ, and γ subunits.
source: There are seven distinct HVACCs (CaV1.1 - CaV1.4; CaV2.1 - CaV2.3) which exist in cells as multi-subunit complexes comprising pore-forming α1-subunits assembled with auxiliary proteins which include β, α2-δ, and γ subunits (Zamponi et al., 2015; Buraei and Yang, 2010; Dolphin, 2012).
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about HVACC structure, supported by citations.

claim: The α1 subunit contains the voltage sensor, selectivity filter, and channel pore.
source: HVACCs are named according to the identity of the component α1 subunit (α1A-α1F; α1S) which also contains the voltage sensor, selectivity filter, and channel pore.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about the functional domains of the α1 subunit.

claim: Auxiliary subunits typically regulate HVACC trafficking, gating, and modulation.
source: The various auxiliary subunits typically regulate HVACC trafficking, gating, and modulation, and are recognized as potential targets for developing HVACC-directed therapeutics.
evidence: This is a statement of established knowledge about the function of auxiliary subunits.

claim: Gabapentin targets HVACC α2-δ subunits.
source: For example, gabapentin, which is clinically utilized for treating epilepsy and neuropathic pain, targets HVACC α2-δ subunits (Gee et al., 1996).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous work on gabapentin's mechanism of action.

claim: Heterologous expression experiments indicate that the association of α1 with β is obligatory for the formation of surface-targeted functional HVACCs.
source: Based on the presumption that the association of α1 with β is obligatory for the formation of surface-targeted functional HVACCs as indicated by heterologous expression experiments (Buraei and Yang, 2010), disruption of the α1-β interaction has been long pursued as a strategy to develop HVACC inhibitors (Young et al., 1998; Findeisen et al., 2017; Chen, 2018; Khanna et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work on α1-β interactions.

claim: Disruption of the α1-β interaction has been long pursued as a strategy to develop HVACC inhibitors.
source: Based on the presumption that the association of α1 with β is obligatory for the formation of surface-targeted functional HVACCs as indicated by heterologous expression experiments (Buraei and Yang, 2010), disruption of the α1-β interaction has been long pursued as a strategy to develop HVACC inhibitors (Young et al., 1998; Findeisen et al., 2017; Chen, 2018; Khanna et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work on HVACC inhibitor development strategies.

claim: Over-expression of peptides derived from the α1-interaction domain (AID) has been utilized as putative genetically-encoded HVACC inhibitors.
source: To this end, over-expression of peptides derived from the α1-interaction domain (AID) which contains the amino acid sequence responsible for high-affinity α1-β association (Pragnell et al., 1994; Van Petegem et al., 2004; Chen et al., 2004; Opatowsky et al., 2003), has been utilized by several groups as putative genetically-encoded HVACC inhibitors (Findeisen et al., 2017; Yang et al., 2019).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work on AID peptides as HVACC inhibitors.

claim: Recent data suggests that in some adult tissue the α1-β interaction is not absolutely essential for surface trafficking of HVACCs.
source: However, the efficacy of this approach in vivo may be limited as recent data suggests that in some adult tissue the α1-β interaction is not absolutely essential for surface trafficking of HVACCs (Yang et al., 2019; Meissner et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to recent work on α1-β interactions in adult tissue.

claim: RGK proteins are endogenous small Ras-like G-proteins that profoundly inhibit all HVACCs when over-expressed in either heterologous cells or native tissue.
source: Rad/Rem/Rem2/Gem/Kir (RGK) proteins are endogenous small Ras-like G-proteins that profoundly inhibit all HVACCs when over-expressed in either heterologous cells or native tissue (Béguin et al., 2001; Finlin et al., 2003; Chen et al., 2005; Xu et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work on RGK proteins.

claim: RGK proteins form ternary complexes with HVACCs via binding to constituent β subunits.
source: They form ternary complexes with HVACCs via binding to constituent β subunits and inhibit currents via multiple mechanisms including removal of surface channels and impairing gating (Yang and Colecraft, 2013; Yang et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work on RGK protein mechanisms.

claim: RGK proteins inhibit currents via multiple mechanisms including removal of surface channels and impairing gating.
source: They form ternary complexes with HVACCs via binding to constituent β subunits and inhibit currents via multiple mechanisms including removal of surface channels and impairing gating (Yang and Colecraft, 2013; Yang et al., 2010).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work on RGK protein mechanisms.

claim: Utility of RGKs as genetically-encoded HVACC inhibitors is confounded by potential off-target effects since they interact with and regulate other binding partners such as cytoskeletal proteins, 14-3-3, calmodulin, and CaM kinase II.
source: Despite their efficacy, utility of RGKs as genetically-encoded HVACC inhibitors is confounded by potential off-target effects since they interact with and regulate other binding partners such as cytoskeletal proteins, 14-3-3, calmodulin, and CaM kinase II (Yang and Colecraft, 2013; Correll et al., 2008; Royer et al., 2018; Béguin et al., 2005; Ward et al., 2004).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work on RGK protein interactions.

claim: Purified CaVβ1 and CaVβ3 were used for llama immunization.
source: Purified β1 and β3 (1 mg each) were used for llama immunization, and successful serum conversion was confirmed by ELISA (not shown).
evidence: The manuscript describes the experimental procedure for llama immunization.

claim: At least seven distinct classes of nanobody binders were identified based on unique sequences within complementarity determining regions (CDR1-3).
source: We identified at least seven distinct classes of nanobody binders based on the unique sequences within complementarity determining regions (CDR1-3), the major determinants of antigen binding (Figure 1d,e).
evidence: The manuscript presents sequence alignment data showing distinct CDR3 sequences.

claim: Nb.F3 binds all four CaVβ isoforms (β1-β4) in cells.
source: Similar experiments conducted with the other CaVβs (β2-β4) showed that they all bind with nb.F3-CFP-C1 in cells (Figure 1f; Figure 1—figure supplement 1), indicating the nanobody interacts with an epitope conserved among CaVβs.
evidence: The manuscript presents co-translocation assay data showing nb.F3 binding to all CaVβ isoforms.

claim: Nb.F3 interacts with an epitope conserved among CaVβs.
source: Similar experiments conducted with the other CaVβs (β2-β4) showed that they all bind with nb.F3-CFP-C1 in cells (Figure 1f; Figure 1—figure supplement 1), indicating the nanobody interacts with an epitope conserved among CaVβs.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that nb.F3 binds all four CaVβ isoforms.

claim: Isothermal titration calorimetry using purified nb.F3 and CaVβ2b indicated a high-affinity (Kd = 13.2 ± 7.2 nM) interaction and a 1:1 stoichiometry.
source: Isothermal titration calorimetry using purified nb.F3 and CaVβ2b indicated a high-affinity (Kd = 13.2 ± 7.2 nM) interaction and a 1:1 stoichiometry (Figure 1g).
evidence: The manuscript presents ITC data showing the binding affinity and stoichiometry.

claim: Nb.F3 had no impact on surface or total expression of BBS-α1B-YFP co-expressed with β1b.
source: In cells expressing BBS-α1B-YFP and β1b, nb.F3 had no impact on Alexa647 or YFP fluorescence compared to control (Figure 2b–d), indicating no disruption of channel trafficking or effect on α1B expression.
evidence: The manuscript presents flow cytometry data showing no change in surface or total channel levels.

claim: Nb.F3 had no impact on whole-cell Ba2+ currents from CaV2.2 channels reconstituted with β1b.
source: Cells expressing α1B + β1b + α2δ displayed robust whole-cell Ba2+ currents that were completely unaffected by nb.F3 (Figure 2i; Ipeak,0mV = −104.4 ± 22.0 pA/pF, n = 10 for CFP, and Ipeak,0mV = −103.5 ± 39.5 pA/pF, n = 10 for nb.F3).
evidence: The manuscript presents electrophysiology data showing no change in current amplitude.

claim: Nb.F3 had no impact on whole-cell Ba2+ currents from CaV2.2 channels reconstituted with β2, β3, or β4.
source: A similar lack of effect of nb.F3 was observed on currents from either CaV2.2 reconstituted with the other β2-β4 subunits (Figure 2j-l), or CaV1.2 (α1C + β2a + α2δ) channels (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The manuscript presents electrophysiology data showing no change in current amplitude for different β subunits.

claim: Nb.F3 had no impact on whole-cell Ba2+ currents from CaV1.2 channels.
source: A similar lack of effect of nb.F3 was observed on currents from either CaV2.2 reconstituted with the other β2-β4 subunits (Figure 2j-l), or CaV1.2 (α1C + β2a + α2δ) channels (Figure 2—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The manuscript presents electrophysiology data showing no change in current amplitude for CaV1.2.

claim: Nb.F3-Nedd4L significantly suppressed surface density of BBS-α1B irrespective of the identity of the co-expressed YFP-tagged CaVβ.
source: By contrast, nb.F3-Nedd4L significantly suppressed surface density of BBS-α1B irrespective of the identity of the co-expressed YFP-tagged CaVβ (Figure 3c, red bars; Figure 3—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript presents flow cytometry data showing decreased surface channel levels.

claim: The decreased BBS-α1B surface density by nb.F3-Nedd4L requires the catalytic activity of the attached Nedd4L HECT domain.
source: The decreased BBS-α1B surface density was not observed with nb.F3-Nedd4L[C942S] (Figure 3c, green bars), indicating it requires the catalytic activity of the attached Nedd4L HECT domain.
evidence: The manuscript presents flow cytometry data showing that the catalytically dead mutant does not reduce surface channels.

claim: Nb.F3-Nedd4L strongly reduced CaV1.2 surface density in a ubiquitin-dependent manner.
source: Similarly, in cells expressing BBS-α1C + βX-YFP, nb.F3-Nedd4L strongly reduced CaV1.2 surface density in a ubiquitin-dependent manner (Figure 3—figure supplement 2).
evidence: The manuscript presents flow cytometry data showing decreased CaV1.2 surface levels.

claim: Nb.F3-Nedd4L had no significant impact on total α1B subunit expression.
source: Similar to our observations for CaVβ, nb.F3-NeddL had no significant impact on the expression of BBS-α1B-YFP (Figure 3e, red bars) relative to either negative controls (black bars) or cells expressing nb.F3-Nedd4L[C942S] (green bars).
evidence: The manuscript presents flow cytometry data showing no change in total α1B levels.

claim: Nb.F3-Nedd4L essentially eliminated CaV2.2 currents reconstituted from α1B + α2δ co-expressed with any of the four CaVβs.
source: Remarkably, nb.F3-Nedd4L essentially eliminated CaV2.2 currents reconstituted from α1B + α2δ co-expressed with any of the four CaVβs (Figure 3g-j).
evidence: The manuscript presents electrophysiology data showing near-complete elimination of currents.

claim: Nb.F3-Nedd4L was equally effective in ablating whole-cell currents in reconstituted CaV1.2, CaV1.3, CaV2.1, and CaV2.3 channels.
source: Further, nb.F3-Nedd4L was equally effective in ablating whole-cell currents in reconstituted CaV1.2, CaV1.3, CaV2.1, and CaV2.3 channels (Figure 4).
evidence: The manuscript presents electrophysiology data showing elimination of currents from multiple HVACC types.

claim: CaV-aβlator virtually eliminated CaV1.2 currents in cultured adult guinea pig ventricular cardiomyocytes.
source: By contrast, in contemporaneous experiments, cardiomyocytes expressing CaV-aβlator via adenovirus-mediated infection displayed virtually no CaV1.2 currents, demonstrating an exceptional CaV-aβlation efficiency in this system (Figure 5a,b; Ipeak,0mV = −1.0 ± 0.3 pA/pF, n = 9).
evidence: The manuscript presents electrophysiology data from cardiomyocytes showing near-complete elimination of L-type calcium currents.

claim: Ubiquitination is necessary for CaV-aβlation in cardiomyocytes.
source: Cardiomyocytes expressing nb.F3-Nedd4L[C942S] displayed ICa,L similar to control (Ipeak,0mV = −5.1 ± 0.6 pA/pF, n = 10), indicating that ubiquitination is necessary for CaV-aβlation in this system.
evidence: The manuscript presents electrophysiology data showing that the catalytically dead mutant does not eliminate currents.

claim: CaV-aβlator caused a redistribution of α1C from dyadic junctions in cardiomyocytes.
source: However, there was a redistribution of α1C from dyadic junctions, as reported by a dramatic loss of co-localization between α1C and RyR2 (Figure 5c).
evidence: The manuscript presents immunofluorescence data showing decreased colocalization of α1C with RyR2.

claim: The punctate α1C signals in CaV-aβlator-expressing cardiomyocytes coincided with Rab7 immunofluorescence signals.
source: Rather, the punctate α1C signals in CaV-aβlator-expressing cardiomyocytes coincided with Rab7, but not Rab5 or LAMP1, immunofluorescence signals (Figure 5d; Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript presents immunofluorescence data showing increased colocalization of α1C with Rab7.

claim: The mechanism of CaV-aβlator inhibition of ICa,L is redistribution of α1C from dyadic junctions to intracellular compartments, specifically Rab7-positive late endosomes.
source: Thus, the mechanism of CaV-aβlator inhibition of ICa,L is redistribution of α1C from dyadic junctions to intracellular compartments, specifically Rab7-positive late endosomes (Figure 5h) (Rink et al., 2005).
evidence: This is inferred from the immunofluorescence data showing redistribution of α1C to Rab7-positive compartments.

claim: CaV-aβlator substantially increased ubiquitination of both α1C and CaVβ1b subunits.
source: Indeed, in pulldown experiments of recombinant CaV1.2 channels, CaV-aβlator substantially increased ubiquitination of both α1C (Figure 5e,f) and CaVβ1b subunits (Figure 5g).
evidence: The manuscript presents pulldown and western blot data showing increased ubiquitination.

claim: The overall levels of α1C expression was unchanged with CaV-aβlator despite the increased ubiquitination.
source: Nevertheless, the overall levels of α1C expression was unchanged with CaV-aβlator despite the increased ubiquitination (Figure 5e).
evidence: The manuscript presents western blot data showing no change in total α1C levels.

claim: Direct ubiquitination of α1C by CaV-aβlator may underlie the redistribution of CaV1.2 channels from dyads to Rab7-positive late endosomes.
source: Taken together, our results suggest that direct ubiquitination of α1C by CaV-aβlator may underlie the redistribution of CaV1.2 channels from dyads to Rab7-positive late endosomes (Figure 5h).
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on the observed ubiquitination and redistribution data.

claim: Depolarization-induced Ca2+ influx was virtually eliminated in DRG neurons expressing CaV-aβlator.
source: By contrast, depolarization-induced Ca2+ influx was virtually eliminated in neurons expressing CaV-ablator, demonstrating highly efficient CaV-ablation in this system (Figure 6a,b).
evidence: The manuscript presents calcium imaging data showing elimination of KCl-evoked calcium transients.

claim: CaV-aβlator selectively eliminates HVACCs in DRG neurons without impacting LVA T-type channels.
source: Overall, these results indicate CaV-ablator selectively eliminates HVACCs in DRG neurons without impacting LVA T-type channels.
evidence: The manuscript presents electrophysiology data showing elimination of HVACC currents while T-type currents remain.

claim: Control pancreatic β-cells expressing GFP or nb.F3-Nedd4L[C942S] displayed robust glucose- or KCl-evoked fura-2-reported Ca2+ transients that were essentially abolished in cells expressing CaV-aβlator.
source: Control cells expressing GFP or nb.F3-Nedd4L[C942S] displayed robust glucose- or KCl-evoked fura-2-reported Ca2+ transients that were essentially abolished in cells expressing CaV-aβlator (Figure 6e-g).
evidence: The manuscript presents calcium imaging data showing elimination of glucose- and KCl-evoked calcium transients.

claim: CaV-aβlator is a potent genetically-encoded HVACC inhibitor that is effective across diverse cellular contexts.
source: Altogether, these results reveal the exceptional activity of CaV-aβlator as a genetically-encoded HVACC inhibitor that is effective across diverse cellular contexts.
evidence: This is a summary statement based on the data presented from multiple cell types.

claim: CaV-aβlator combines the exquisite specificity of a CaVβ-targeted nanobody and the powerfully consequential catalytic activity of an E3 ubiquitin ligase.
source: CaV-aβlator combines the exquisite specificity of a CaVβ-targeted nanobody and the powerfully consequential catalytic activity of an E3 ubiquitin ligase.
evidence: This is a summary statement describing the design of CaV-aβlator.

claim: In cells expressing both LVACCs and HVACCs, the physiological effects mediated specifically through LVACCs versus HVACCs in vivo can be difficult to decipher.
source: In cells expressing both classes of channels, the physiological effects mediated specifically through LVACCs versus HVACCs in vivo can be difficult to decipher.
evidence: This is a general statement about the challenges in studying calcium channel function.

claim: CaV-aβlator can be deployed in target cells to virtually erase all HVACCs while leaving LVACC actions intact.
source: CaV-aβlator now presents as a tool that can be deployed in target cells to virtually erase all HVACCs while leaving LVACC actions intact.
evidence: This is based on the data showing selective elimination of HVACCs but not T-type channels in DRG neurons.

claim: RGK GTPases are capable of potently inhibiting CaV1/CaV2 channels when over-expressed in target cells.
source: The closest existing proteins that can similarly eliminate HVACCs are RGK GTPases which are capable of potently inhibiting CaV1/CaV2 channels when over-expressed in target cells (Murata et al., 2004; Chen et al., 2005; Xu et al., 2010; Puckerin et al., 2018; Bannister et al., 2008).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work on RGK proteins.

claim: A distinct disadvantage of RGKs is their propensity for off-target effects due to their known interactions with cytoskeletal proteins and other signaling molecules.
source: However, a distinct disadvantage of RGKs is their propensity for off-target effects due to their known interactions with, and regulation of, cytoskeletal proteins and other signaling molecules including 14-3-3, calmodulin, and CaM kinase II (Yang and Colecraft, 2013; Correll et al., 2008; Royer et al., 2018; Béguin et al., 2005).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work on RGK protein interactions.

claim: Over-expressing the AID peptide in adult cardiac myocytes is not effective in inhibiting CaV1.2 channels.
source: Indeed, over-expressing the AID peptide in adult cardiac myocytes is not effective in inhibiting CaV1.2 channels (Yang et al., 2019), because in this context α1C binding to CaVβ is not absolutely required for channel trafficking to the surface (Yang et al., 2019; Meissner et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work on AID peptides in cardiomyocytes.

claim: In adult cardiomyocytes, α1C binding to CaVβ is not absolutely required for channel trafficking to the surface.
source: Indeed, over-expressing the AID peptide in adult cardiac myocytes is not effective in inhibiting CaV1.2 channels (Yang et al., 2019), because in this context α1C binding to CaVβ is not absolutely required for channel trafficking to the surface (Yang et al., 2019; Meissner et al., 2011).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work on α1C trafficking in cardiomyocytes.

claim: The ability of CaV-aβlator to essentially eradicate ICa,L in adult cardiomyocytes indicates that under normal physiological conditions essentially all α1C subunits are associated with a CaVβ in ventricular heart cells.
source: Nevertheless, the ability of CaV-aβlator to essentially eradicate ICa,L in adult cardiomyocytes indicates that under normal physiological conditions essentially all α1C subunits are associated with a CaVβ in ventricular heart cells.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that CaV-aβlator, which targets CaVβ, eliminates essentially all ICa,L.

claim: Targeted ubiquitination of α1C/β2 complexes in cardiomyocytes with CaV-aβlator specifically arrests CaV1.2 channels in Rab7-positive late endosomes.
source: Here, we show that targeted ubiquitination of α1C/β2 complexes in cardiomyocytes with CaV-aβlator specifically arrests CaV1.2 channels in Rab7-positive late endosomes.
evidence: This is based on the immunofluorescence data showing redistribution of α1C to Rab7-positive compartments.

claim: The HECT domain of Nedd4L principally catalyzes the addition of K63-linkage polyubiquitin chains to target proteins.
source: CaV-aβlator possesses the catalytic HECT domain of Nedd4L which is known to principally catalyze the addition of K63-linkage polyubiquitin chains to target proteins (Kim and Huibregtse, 2009; Scheffner and Kumar, 2014).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work on Nedd4L catalytic activity.

claim: K63-ubiquitin chains on α1C/β2 subunits may be a key signal directing CaV1.2 channels to late endosomes.
source: Thus, our results suggest that K63-ubiquitin chains on α1C/β2 subunits may be a key signal directing CaV1.2 channels to late endosomes.
evidence: This is a speculative statement based on the known activity of Nedd4L and the observed redistribution.

claim: Targeted ubiquitination of HVACC α1 subunits with CaV-aβlator did not lead to their enhanced degradation either in heterologous cells or cardiomyocytes.
source: We further found that targeted ubiquitination of HVACC α1 subunits with CaV-aβlator did not lead to their enhanced degradation either in heterologous cells or cardiomyocytes.
evidence: This is based on the flow cytometry and immunofluorescence data showing no change in total α1 levels.

claim: Using a GFP nanobody to target the Nedd4L HECT domain to YFP-tagged KCNQ1 resulted in reduced expression of this K+ channel pore-forming α1 subunit.
source: By contrast, using a GFP nanobody to target the Nedd4L HECT domain to YFP-tagged KCNQ1, a known substrate of endogenous Nedd4L, resulted in reduced expression of this K+ channel pore-forming α1 subunit (Kanner et al., 2017).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous work on KCNQ1.

claim: The impact of Nedd4L HECT domain on the stability of membrane proteins is likely substrate-dependent.
source: Hence, the impact of Nedd4L HECT domain on the stability of membrane proteins is likely substrate-dependent.
evidence: This is inferred from the different effects on CaV channels versus KCNQ1.

claim: Blocking the activity of specific HVACCs with small molecules is a prevailing or potential therapy for many cardiovascular and neurological diseases including pain, hypertension, cardiac arrhythmias, epilepsy, and Parkinson's disease.
source: Blocking the activity of specific HVACCs with small molecules is a prevailing or potential therapy for many cardiovascular and neurological diseases including; pain, hypertension, cardiac arrhythmias, epilepsy, and Parkinson's disease (Zamponi, 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to a review on HVACC therapeutics.

claim: A limitation of small molecule or toxin blockers for HVACCs is the propensity for off-target effects due to their inevitable widespread distribution when administered to a patient.
source: A limitation of small molecule or toxin blockers for HVACCs is the propensity for off-target effects due to their inevitable widespread distribution when administered to a patient.
evidence: This is a general statement about the pharmacological properties of small molecule drugs.

claim: Genetically-encoded HVACC inhibitors have great potential to be useful therapeutics with the advantage that their expression can be restricted to target tissues/cell types.
source: Genetically-encoded HVACC inhibitors have great potential to be useful therapeutics with the advantage that their expression can be restricted to target tissues/cell types, or even to spatially discrete channels within single cells (Murata et al., 2004; Makarewich et al., 2012).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work on genetically-encoded inhibitors.

claim: CaV-aβlator could be a lead molecule for future development into a gene therapy for particular applications where a genetically-encoded HVACC inhibitor is warranted.
source: Given its potency in silencing HVACC activity, CaV-aβlator could be a lead molecule for future development into a gene therapy for particular applications where a genetically-encoded HVACC inhibitor is warranted.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential future applications.

claim: CaV1/CaV2 channels of a particular type may form discrete signaling units with different functional outputs in single cells based on their incorporation into divergent macro-molecular complexes.
source: For example, a prevailing idea is that CaV1/CaV2 channels of a particular type (e.g. CaV1.2 channels in cardiomyocytes) may yet form discrete signaling units with different functional outputs in single cells based on their incorporation into divergent macro-molecular complexes (Shaw and Colecraft, 2013).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous work on channel signaling complexes.

claim: Different CaVβ isoforms could be a node of signal diversification by promoting formation of molecularly distinct HVACC macro-molecular complexes.
source: There are tantalizing hints that different CaVβ isoforms could be a node of signal diversification by promoting formation of molecularly distinct HVACC macro-molecular complexes (McEnery et al., 1998; Brice and Dolphin, 1999; Campiglio and Flucher, 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work on CaVβ isoforms.

claim: The ability to inhibit specific CaV channel macro-molecular complexes based on the identity of the constituent CaVβ is biologically important, yet not rigorously addressable with conventional knockout/knockdown approaches.
source: Hence, the ability to inhibit specific CaV channel macro-molecular complexes based on the identity of the constituent CaVβ is biologically important, yet not rigorously addressable with conventional knockout/knockdown approaches.
evidence: This is a statement about the limitations of current approaches and the potential of the new tool.

claim: Development of CaVβ isoform-specific nanobodies should be feasible given that there is sequence divergence among CaVβs outside the conserved src homology 3 (SH3) and guanylate kinase (GK) domains.
source: A challenge to realize this possibility is the development of CaVβ isoform-specific nanobodies which should be feasible given that there is sequence divergence among CaVβs outside the conserved src homology 3 (SH3) and guanylate kinase (GK) domains (Buraei and Yang, 2010).
evidence: This is a speculative statement about future possibilities, supported by a citation about CaVβ structure.

claim: The phenomenon of ion channel pore-forming α1 subunits assembled with diverse auxiliary subunits in individual cells is common throughout biology.
source: In a broader context, the phenomenon of ion channel pore-forming α1 subunits assembled with diverse auxiliary subunits in individual cells is common throughout biology (O'Malley and Isom, 2015; Copits and Swanson, 2012; Trimmer, 2015).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work on ion channel structure.

claim: CaV-aβlator-inspired molecules and approaches might be expected to elucidate functional dimensions of ion channel macro-molecular complex signaling that have remained refractory to analyses.
source: Hence, CaV-aβlator-inspired molecules and approaches might be expected to elucidate functional dimensions of ion channel macro-molecular complex signaling that, to date, have remained refractory to analyses.
evidence: This is a speculative statement about potential future applications of the approach.

claim: Nb.F3 binds CaVβ2b with a 1:1 stoichiometry.
source: Isothermal titration calorimetry using purified nb.F3 and CaVβ2b indicated a high-affinity (Kd = 13.2 ± 7.2 nM) interaction and a 1:1 stoichiometry (Figure 1g).
evidence: The ITC data shows N = 0.93 ± 0.02, indicating 1:1 stoichiometry.

claim: Application of 1 μM phorbol-12,13-dibutyrate (PdBu) led to the rapid and dramatic redistribution of nb.F3-CFP-C1 from the cytosol to the plasma and nuclear membranes.
source: Application of 1 μM phorbol-12,13-dibutyrate (PdBu) led to the rapid and dramatic redistribution of nb.F3-CFP-C1 from the cytosol to the plasma and nuclear membranes (Figure 1f).
evidence: The manuscript presents confocal imaging data showing membrane translocation upon PdBu treatment.

claim: YFP-β1 concomitantly redistributed to the plasma and nuclear membranes upon PdBu treatment, confirming it associates with nb.F3 inside cells.
source: Reassuringly, YFP-β1 concomitantly redistributed to the plasma and nuclear membranes, providing a convenient visual confirmation that it associates with nb.F3 inside cells (Figure 1f).
evidence: The manuscript presents confocal imaging data showing co-translocation of YFP-β1 with nb.F3-CFP-C1.

claim: Neither F3-Nedd4L nor F3-Nedd4L[C942S] had any significant impact on β1b total expression.
source: In cells expressing BBS-α1B + β1b-YFP + α2δ, neither F3-Nedd4L nor F3-Nedd4L[C942S] had any significant impact on β1b total expression as reported by the unchanged YFP fluorescence compared to negative control cells (Figure 3a,b).
evidence: The manuscript presents flow cytometry data showing no change in YFP fluorescence.

claim: The expression levels of β2 and β3 were modestly reduced by nb.F3, although this effect did not reach statistical significance.
source: The expression levels of β1-YFP and β4-YFP were unaffected by nb.F3, whereas the levels of β2 and β3 were modestly reduced (although this effect did not reach statistical significance), suggesting a possible slightly increased vulnerability of these two isoforms to degradation when bound by the nanobody (Figure 2h).
evidence: The manuscript presents flow cytometry data showing a trend towards lower β2 and β3 levels.

claim: Cultured adult guinea pig ventricular cardiomyocytes retain the rod-shaped phenotype and overall cyto-architecture of freshly isolated heart cells.
source: We used adenovirus to express CaV-aβlator or nb.F3-Nedd4L[C942S] in CAGPVCs which retain the rod-shaped phenotype and overall cyto-architecture of freshly isolated heart cells (Figure 5a).
evidence: The manuscript presents confocal images showing rod-shaped cardiomyocytes.

claim: Control (non-infected) cardiomyocytes expressed ICa,L that peaked at a 0 mV test pulse.
source: Control (non-infected) cardiomyocytes expressed ICa,L that peaked at a 0 mV test pulse (Figure 5a,b; Ipeak,0mV = −6.5 ± 0.2 pA/pF, n = 8).
evidence: The manuscript presents electrophysiology data showing the voltage dependence of ICa,L.

claim: CaV-aβlator expressing cardiomyocytes showed no difference in total CaVβ2 levels as compared to either uninfected or nb.F3-Nedd4L[C942S]-expressing cells.
source: Cardiomyocytes expressing CaV-aβlator also showed no difference in total CaVβ2 levels as compared to either uninfected or nb.F3-Nedd4L[C942S]-expressing cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1).
evidence: The manuscript presents immunofluorescence data showing no change in total β2 levels.

claim: The signal intensity for punctate α1C staining was unchanged in CaV-aβlator expressing cardiomyocytes compared to control cells.
source: In cardiomyocytes expressing CaV-aβlator, the signal intensity for punctate α1C staining was unchanged from control cells (Figure 5—figure supplement 1), suggesting no impact of the presumed increase in ubiquitination on the stability of the protein.
evidence: The manuscript presents immunofluorescence data showing no change in total α1C levels.

claim: Murine dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons express multiple CaV1/CaV2 channel types.
source: We next tested the efficacy of CaV-aβlator to suppress HVACCs in murine dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons which were of interest because they express multiple CaV1/CaV2 channel types (Murali et al., 2015; McCallum et al., 2011), and also play a key role in the processing of noxious signals including pain and itch (Han et al., 2013; Kim et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work on DRG neuron channel expression.

claim: DRG neurons play a key role in the processing of noxious signals including pain and itch.
source: We next tested the efficacy of CaV-aβlator to suppress HVACCs in murine dorsal root ganglion (DRG) neurons which were of interest because they express multiple CaV1/CaV2 channel types (Murali et al., 2015; McCallum et al., 2011), and also play a key role in the processing of noxious signals including pain and itch (Han et al., 2013; Kim et al., 2016).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work on DRG neuron function.

claim: Murine pancreatic β-cells have multiple CaV channel types (CaV1.2, CaV1.3, and CaV2.1) involved in insulin release.
source: Finally, we tested whether CaV-ablator is also effective in murine pancreatic β-cells, which have multiple CaV channel types (CaV1.2, CaV1.3, and CaV2.1) involved in insulin release (Yang and Berggren, 2006).
evidence: This statement is supported by a citation to previous work on pancreatic β-cell calcium channels.

claim: In adult cardiomyocytes, binding of α1C to CaVβ is not obligatory for substantive CaV1.2 channel trafficking to the surface sarcolemma.
source: Moreover, as it has now been shown that in adult cardiomyocytes binding of α1C to CaVβ is not obligatory for substantive CaV1.2 channel trafficking to the surface sarcolemma (Yang et al., 2019; Meissner et al., 2011), the fraction of CaVβ-bound CaV1.2 channels contributing to the whole-cell L-type current (ICa,L) in ventricular myocytes is ambiguous.
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work on α1C-β interactions in cardiomyocytes.

claim: The fraction of CaVβ-bound CaV1.2 channels contributing to the whole-cell L-type current (ICa,L) in ventricular myocytes is ambiguous.
source: Moreover, as it has now been shown that in adult cardiomyocytes binding of α1C to CaVβ is not obligatory for substantive CaV1.2 channel trafficking to the surface sarcolemma (Yang et al., 2019; Meissner et al., 2011), the fraction of CaVβ-bound CaV1.2 channels contributing to the whole-cell L-type current (ICa,L) in ventricular myocytes is ambiguous.
evidence: This is inferred from the observation that α1C-β binding is not obligatory for trafficking.

claim: CaVα1C in uninfected cardiomyocytes presented with a characteristic striated punctate distribution pattern that co-localized with that of ryanodine (RyR2) receptors.
source: CaVα1C in uninfected cardiomyocytes presented with a characteristic striated punctate distribution pattern that co-localized with that of ryanodine (RyR2) receptors (Figure 5c), reflecting their well-known predominant localization at dyadic junctions (Scriven et al., 2000; Bers, 2002).
evidence: The manuscript presents immunofluorescence data showing colocalization of α1C with RyR2.

claim: The colocalization of α1C with RyR2 reflects their well-known predominant localization at dyadic junctions.
source: CaVα1C in uninfected cardiomyocytes presented with a characteristic striated punctate distribution pattern that co-localized with that of ryanodine (RyR2) receptors (Figure 5c), reflecting their well-known predominant localization at dyadic junctions (Scriven et al., 2000; Bers, 2002).
evidence: This statement is supported by citations to previous work on CaV1.2 and RyR2 localization.

claim: Rab7 is a marker of late endosomes.
source: Thus, the mechanism of CaV-aβlator inhibition of ICa,L is redistribution of α1C from dyadic junctions to intracellular compartments, specifically Rab7-positive late endosomes (Figure 5h) (Rink et al., 2005).
evidence: This is established knowledge in cell biology, supported by the citation.
